newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures begin pit trading softer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures begin pit trading softer.

text.p: U.S. debt futures began pit trading softer in quiet trade.
The market continued to drift in the absence of fresh, critical U.S. economic data until next week.
Brokers said the 0.2-percent rise in weekly BTM/Schroders chain store sales was slightly smaller than the 0.5-percent increase some pundits had forecast, but it had muted effect.

Nor did gains in the dollar elicit much response. The dollar rose overseas to as high as 1.7088 marks after a report from Germany's six leading economic research institutes that said the dollar on average in 1998 will be 1.80 marks.

Also out Tuesday are March U.S. import/export prices, due at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT, and weekly Redbook retail sales, due Tuesday afternoon. Early Tuesday evening, Richmond Federal Reserve President Alfred Broaddus will address financial executives in Virginia.
Focus instead riveted on technicals and supplies, brokers said.

Treasury will sell $17.0 billion in two-year notes Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes Wednesday. Some brokers wondered whether Monday's downdrift would continue if players tried to cheapen issues before the auctions.
But others said the two-year already appeared relatively well-priced to draw demand.
"The rumors are that it (two-year sale) will be fairly well-received," said the floor broker. "It's fairly cheap."
Floor brokers said order flow was thin in Treasury bonds although small sales weighed slightly on the 10-year note.
They said June bonds could stick range-bound until better indications emerged about how two-year demand was shaping up but said futures could firm if shorts got frustrated.
"The weaker shorts could bail out and we could see 27-31 (107-27/32 - 31/32)," added the floor broker.
A second broker tied a subsequent rise in June T-bonds to 107-24/32 to shortcovering when selling lacked followthrough. But he looked for further gains to attract sellers again.
"I still expect some shorts to come in between 26 and 29 (107-26/32 - 29/32)," he said.
Stiff resistance loomed at 108-06/32 - 7/32, which encompasses last week's and Monday's highs. On the downside, initial support was dotted from 107-17/32 to 107-13/32.

At 0820 CDT/1320 GMT, June bonds rose 2/32 to 107-23/32, notes rose 1/32 at 105-28/32, munis added 5/32 to 112-24/32, Sept bulls fell 0.015 at 94.320, Euros lost 0.015 to 93.735. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
